questions.question: Find the number which is NOT a prime number.
questions.solution:
**Concept used:**

Prime numbers are natural numbers that are divisible by only 1 and the number itself.

The no. of factors of the prime number is 1 and the number itself.

1) Factors of 89 = 1 × 89

2) Factors of 87 = 3 × 29

3) Factors of 79 = 1 × 79

4) Factors of 97 = 1 × 97

Hence, the correct answer is** "87".**

questions.question: The diameter of the driving wheel of a cart is 154 cm. Calculate the revolution per minute [RPM] of the wheel (approx) in order to keep a speed of 33 Kilo meter per hour.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Diameter of the wheel = 154 cm

Radius of the wheel = 154/2 = 77 cm

Speed = 33km/h

**Formula used:**

Circumference of a circle = 2πr

where r → radius of a circle

Distance covered = speed × time

**Calculation:**

Distance covered in one revolution = Circumference of wheel

⇒ 2πr = 2 × 22/7 × 77 = 484 cm

Speed = 33 km/hr = 33 × 100000/60 = 55000 cm/min

∴ Total Revolutions covered in one min

⇒ 55000/484 = 113.63 ≈ 114

questions.question: A number is divided into two parts in such a way that 30% of first part is 25 more than the 20% of second part. 50% of second part is 33.5 more than the 60% of first part. What is the number?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Let the two parts of no. is a and b and the no. is (a + b)

From the question,

30% of a = 20% of b + 25

⇒ 3/10 × a = 1/5 × b + 25

⇒ 3a = 2b + 250

Again, from the question

50% of b = 60% of a + 33.5

⇒ 1/2 × b = 3/5 × a + 25

⇒ 5b – 6a = 335

⇒ 5b – 2 × 3a = 335

⇒ 5b – 2 × (2b + 250) = 335

⇒ 5b – 4b – 500 = 335

⇒ b = 835

So, 3a = 2b + 250 = 2 × 835 + 250 = 1920

⇒ a = 640

**Hence, a + b = 640 + 835 = 1475**

questions.question: Two vessels of equal capacity contains juice and water in the ratio of 5 ∶ 1 and 5 ∶ 7 respectively. The mixture of both the vessels are mixed and transferred into a bigger vessel. What is the ratio of juice and water in the new mixture?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Vessel 1 capacity = 5 + 1 = 6 units, and Vessel 2 capacity = 5 + 7 = 12 units.

To make the capacities equal, multiply the ratio of Vessel 1 by 2 (since LCM is 12).

Adjusted Vessel 1 = 10 ∶ 2, and Vessel 2 = 5 ∶ 7.

Mix both vessels directly: Total Juice = 10 + 5 = 15, Total Water = 2 + 7 = 9.

Resultant ratio = 15 ∶ 9 = 5 ∶ 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 ∶ 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of juice and water in Vessel 1 = 5 ∶ 1

Ratio of juice and water in Vessel 2 = 5 ∶ 7

Both vessels are of equal capacity.

**Formula / Concept Used:**

When mixing two mixtures of equal quantity, make the sum of parts in both ratios equal by multiplying with appropriate integers before adding corresponding parts.

 
 
 

 
 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 Vessel 1
 J ∶ W = 5 ∶ 1 (Sum=6)
 ×2 → J ∶ W = 10 ∶ 2
 
 Vessel 2
 J ∶ W = 5 ∶ 7 (Sum=12)
 ×1 → J ∶ W = 5 ∶ 7
 
 New Mixture
 J = 10+5, W = 2+7
 Ratio = 15 ∶ 9 = 5 ∶ 3

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of ratio parts in Vessel 1 = 5 + 1 = 6 units.

⇒ Sum of ratio parts in Vessel 2 = 5 + 7 = 12 units.

⇒ LCM of 6 and 12 is 12.

⇒ To make capacities equal, multiply Vessel 1's ratio by (12 ÷ 6) = 2.

⇒ Adjusted ratio of juice and water in Vessel 1 = (5 × 2) ∶ (1 × 2) = 10 ∶ 2

⇒ Adjusted ratio of juice and water in Vessel 2 = 5 ∶ 7

⇒ Total juice in the new mixture = 10 + 5 = 15 units

⇒ Total water in the new mixture = 2 + 7 = 9 units

⇒ Required ratio of juice to water = 15 ∶ 9

⇒ Simplifying the ratio by dividing by 3, we get 5 ∶ 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 ∶ 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mixing Multiple Volumes

If mixtures are mixed in a specific volume ratio (e.g., 2 ∶ 3), first equalize their capacities using the LCM, then multiply by the given volume ratio before adding the respective components together.

Alligation Method

When two mixtures are combined to form a final mixture, the rule of alligation can be applied on the fractional concentration of a single component (either juice or water) to easily find the required mixing ratio.

Replacement Method

When 'x' volume of a mixture is replaced by one of its pure components, the final concentration of the remaining component is given by Final = Initial × (1 − x/V)ⁿ, where V is total volume and n is the number of replacements.

questions.question: In an alloy, aluminium and tin are in the ratio of 4 ∶ 5. In the second alloy, the ratio of same elements is 4 ∶ 7. If equal quantities of these two alloys be mixed to form a new alloy, then what will be the ratio of both of these elements in the new alloy?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

In 1st alloy, the ratio of aluminium and tin = 4 : 5

In 2nd alloy, the ratio of aluminium and tin = 4 : 7

**Calculation:**

Let the quantity of both the alloys are p kg

Total quantity of aluminium = (4p/9 + 4p/11) = 80p/99

Total quantity of tin = (5p/9 + 7p/11) = 118p/99

∴ Required ratio = 80p/99 ∶ 118p/99 = 80 ∶ 118

questions.question: Among four bags, the average weight of the last three bags is 18 kg and the average weight of the first three bags is 19 kg. If the weight of the last bag is 22 kg, then what is the weight (in kg) of first bag?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The average weight of the last three bags = 18kg

The average weight of the first three bags = 19 kg

Weight of the last bag = 22kg

**Formula used:**

Average = Sum of observation ÷ No. of observation

**Calculation:**

Let four bags are p, q, r, s

Average weight of the last three bags (q + r + s) = (Total weight of q, r and s)/3

⇒ 18 = (Total weight of q, r and s)/3

Total weight of the last three bags (q + r + s) = 54 kg

Total weight of bags q + r = 54 – weight of bag s = 54 – 22 = 32

Average weight of the first three bags (p + q + r) = (Total weight of p, q and r)/3

⇒ 19 = (Total weight of p, q and r)/3

Total weight of the first three bags (p + q + r) = 57 kg

∴ Weight of the first bag p = 57 – total weight of bags (q + r)

⇒ 57 – 32 = 25

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**Sum of weight of first three bags = 19 × 3 = 57kg

Sum of weight of all four bags = 57kg + 22kg = 79kg

Sum of weight of last three bag = 18 × 3 = 54kg

So, the weight of 1st bag = sum of weight of all four bags - Sum of weight of last three bag

⇒ 79kg - 54kg = 25kg

questions.question: A sum becomes Rs. 8800 in 4 years at simple interest at the yearly interest rate of 25% per annum. What is the sum (in Rs.)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Amount = Rs. 8000

Time = 4 years

Rate = 25%

**Formula used:**

Amount = Principal + S.I.

S.I. = (P × R × T)/100

where P → Principal

R → Rate of interest

T → Time period

**Calculation:**

S.I. = (P × R × T)/100

⇒ 8800 – P = (P × 25 × 4)/100

⇒ 8800 – P = P

⇒ 2P = 8800

∴ P = 4400

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**Let P = 100%

Interest for 4 years = 25 × 4 = 100%

Amount = 200%

⇒ 200% = Rs.8800

⇒ 100% = Rs.4400

A work can be completed by 18 boys in 24 days. If 6 boys leave after working for 12 days, then how many days will be needed to complete the remaining work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Manpower M₁ = 18

Time taken = 24 days

**Calculation:**

6 boys leave after 12 working days, then manpower for the first 12 days M₂ = 18 and remaining manpower for D₃ days ie. M₃ = 18 – 6 = 12

M₁ × D₁ = M₂ × D₂ + M₃ × D₃

⇒ 18 × 24 = 18 × 12 + 12 × D₃

⇒ 432 = 216 + 12 × D₃

⇒ 12 × D₃ = 216

∴ D₃ = 18 days

questions.question: Two trains are moving in the same direction at the speed of 42 km/hr and 84 km/hr and their lengths are 320 meters and 380 meters respectively. What is the time taken (in seconds) by faster train to cross the slower train?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total distance to cross = 380 + 320 = 700 m

Relative speed (same direction) = 84 − 42 = 42 km/hr

Relative speed in m/s = 42 × (5 / 18) = 35 / 3 m/s

Time taken = Distance ÷ Relative Speed = 700 ÷ (35 / 3) = 60 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 60 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the faster train (L₁) = 380 m

Speed of the faster train (S₁) = 84 km/hr

Length of the slower train (L₂) = 320 m

Speed of the slower train (S₂) = 42 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Time taken to cross = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Relative speed (same direction) = S₁ − S₂

Speed in m/s = Speed in km/hr × (5 / 18)

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 
 
 Train 2 (380m)
 
• 
 84 km/hr
 
 
 Train 1 (320m)
 
• 
 42 km/hr
 
 Relative Speed = 84 − 42 = 42 km/hr

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = L₁ + L₂

⇒ Total Distance = 380 + 320 = 700 m

⇒ Relative Speed = 84 − 42 = 42 km/hr

⇒ Relative Speed in m/s = 42 × (5 / 18)

⇒ Relative Speed = 210 / 18 = 35 / 3 m/s

⇒ Time Taken = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed

⇒ Time Taken = 700 ÷ (35 / 3)

⇒ Time Taken = (700 × 3) / 35

⇒ Time Taken = 20 × 3 = 60 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 60 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two objects travel in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds (S₁ − S₂).

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two objects travel in opposite directions towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Conversion of Units

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply the speed by 5/18. Conversely, to convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.
